blocks.text: Quick verdict

SOAX is the stronger network: 155M residential and 33M mobile IPs on one balance, ISP-level targeting on every plan, and protocol support (UDP, QUIC) few rivals match. It is also cheaper for traffic in its Tier 2 and Tier 3 countries. IPRoyal is the better choice for small or irregular US and European workloads, because its gigabytes never expire while SOAX credits lapse after 60 days, and because SOAX's no-fee Sandbox plan charges $5/GB for US traffic. Mobile-heavy and ad-verification teams should choose SOAX.

IPRoyal and SOAX price residential traffic in very different ways. IPRoyal sells gigabytes that never expire, from a single GB upward. SOAX moved in 2026 to prepaid credits whose cost per gigabyte depends on your plan and on the country of the exit IP, and those credits expire after 60 days. SOAX also has a much bigger network with mobile IPs on the same balance and support for UDP and QUIC. This comparison shows when each pricing model works out cheaper and which features justify the difference.

blocks.text: IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal is a value-focused provider best known for residential traffic that never expires. You can buy a single gigabyte, use it over months, and top up when you need to, which suits irregular projects better than monthly allowances. The residential pool is advertised at 32M+ IPs across 195 countries with state and city targeting, and sticky sessions can be requested for up to seven days. IPRoyal also sells ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies and a Web Unblocker billed per successful request.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
SOAX in 2026: what you get

SOAX rebuilt its pricing in 2026 around credits and country tiers. Residential and mobile traffic share one balance and one per-GB rate, and the rate depends on your plan and the country your exit IP is in: US and German traffic costs more than Indian or Filipino traffic. SOAX advertises 155 million residential and 33 million mobile IPs in 195 countries, supports UDP and QUIC as well as SOCKS5, and includes city and ISP targeting on every plan. It discontinued its datacenter and ISP proxies between late 2025 and mid 2026.

Strengths: Residential and mobile on one balance; UDP and QUIC support alongside SOCKS5; Large pool with city and ISP targeting on every plan; Cheap traffic for Tier 2 and Tier 3 countries. Weak spots: Credits expire after 60 days; US traffic is expensive on small plans; Datacenter and ISP proxies were discontinued.
Pricing: IPRoyal vs SOAX

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

SOAX bills prepaid credits. For US (Tier 1) traffic, the no-fee Sandbox plan costs $5/GB, Builder ($200/month) $3/GB, Team ($500/month) $2.20/GB, and Scale ($1,500/month) $1.50/GB; cheaper countries cost less (Tier 3 from $2/GB on Sandbox). Credits expire 60 days after purchase, and SOAX counts traffic in both directions.

At 10 GB a month the two cost almost the same: about $52.50 with IPRoyal against $50 with SOAX. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; SOAX comes to about $300. The sticker price is only half of it. IPRoyal's unused traffic carries forward, while SOAX's does not (credits expire 60 days after they are added), so if your usage swings from month to month IPRoyal can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

SOAX has the bigger advertised network, 155M residential + 33M mobile residential IPs against 32M+ for IPRoyal, roughly 4.8 times larger. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, IPRoyal lists 195 countries and SOAX lists 195. On targeting, IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification), while SOAX offers country, region, city and ISP; ASN and ZIP on Scale plans.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days, and SOAX offers rotating or sticky; mobile sessions up to 60 minutes. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. IPRoyal: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. SOAX: a large pool and its own error headers help debugging. Let price and the countries you need decide.
SERP and rank tracking: SOAX wins. The deciding factor for SOAX: city and ISP targeting for local results. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With IPRoyal: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. With SOAX: mobile IPs on the same balance as residential. Run the same small test on both before committing.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. IPRoyal: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. SOAX: granular location filters. Let price and the countries you need decide.
Ad verification and geo-testing: SOAX. SOAX has the edge here. Why: ISP, ASN and carrier-level targeting. How IPRoyal compares: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts.
Tight budgets: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. How SOAX compares: cheap in Tier 3 countries but pricey for small US jobs.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. SOAX: Paid 3-day trial, 400 MB for $1.99. Verification and payment rules differ too. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. SOAX: Verification for postpaid and enterprise terms. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test IPRoyal and SOAX before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle IPRoyal vs SOAX faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies; SOAX: paid 3-day trial, 400 MB for $1.99).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, IPRoyal comes out ahead in 1, SOAX in 2, and 3 are ties. That makes SOAX the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects, while SOAX is strongest for mobile-first work such as app testing and social platforms. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
